name: Human serotonin transporter / SERT
coordinateFrame: Original deposited PDB Cartesian frame; protein and bound ligands share this frame. No fitted membrane orientation.

ligands.name: Bound escitalopram (68P), crystallographic heavy-atom pose
ligands.note: Hydrogens absent in experimental pose. Bond orders from RCSB Chemical Component Dictionary 68P, which encodes the neutral component; protonation is not determined by this 3.15 Å heavy-atom model.

provenance.publication: Coleman JA, Green EM, Gouaux E. X-ray structures and mechanism of the human serotonin transporter. Nature 532, 334–339 (2016).
provenance.construct: Engineered thermostabilized SERT construct (ts3), truncated termini; antibody chains B and C omitted from this asset.

limitations: Cα backbone is a trace through resolved experimental coordinates, not a solvent-accessible molecular surface.
Missing residues are gaps: segments prevent drawing invented peptide bonds across missing density.
Helix annotations are HELIX records in the deposition; multiple records may describe parts of one transmembrane helix. Do not count these records as separate transmembrane domains.
The ligand-stabilized outward-open structure is a static experimental snapshot; any transport-cycle motion elsewhere in the scene is schematic, not an interpolated minimum-energy path.
At 3.15 Å, hydrogen atoms and solution protonation states are not experimentally resolved.
Crystal construct, bound antibody, detergents, crystal contacts, and mutations distinguish this structure from native full-length SERT in a neuronal membrane.
